title: Separated-source cancellation with finite target inertia
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and stacks, representability and 2-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable morphism properties are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Flatness, local finite presentation, etaleness and properness use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A stack morphism is separated if its relative diagonal is proper. The inertia stack $I_{\mathcal A}$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows given by conjugating isomorphisms. Its projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The set $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the atlas topology [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be algebraic stacks over $k$, let $\mathcal A$ be separated over $k$, and let $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ be finite. For every $k$-morphism $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ is proper; that is, $f$ is separated. More generally, for $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal C$, if $g\circ f$ is separated and $\Delta_g$ is separated then $f$ is separated. The implication needed for the finite-inertia case is that separated inertia $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ implies a separated diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal B/k}$.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), part (3), and Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), part (1); finite inertia is separated by scheme tests (morphisms.tex Tag 01WN).

proof.text: First prove the general cancellation assertion. Put $D=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ and $E=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A$; these are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. The forgetful map $r:D\to E$ is the 2-base change of $\Delta_g$ along $E\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$. Indeed an object of that pullback is $(a_1,a_2,\gamma:g f(a_1)\simeq g f(a_2))$ with a lift $\beta:f(a_1)\simeq f(a_2)$ of $\gamma$; this is precisely the object $(a_1,a_2,\beta)$ of $D$, and the compatibility equations for arrows agree. Forgetting and restoring $\gamma=g(\beta)$ are inverse up to the specified 2-isomorphisms. The diagonal $\Delta_g$ is representable by [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry], so $r$ is representable by base-change stability [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Since $\Delta_g$ is separated, its base change $r$ is separated by [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence]. Also $r\Delta_f=\Delta_{gf}$, including their tautological 2-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), proof of (3), with the cartesian square of Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map).

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to D$, set $V=\mathcal A\times_E T$ and $W=D\times_E T$. These are algebraic spaces because $\Delta_{gf}$ and $r$ are representable, the former by [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry] and the latter by step 1. We have $V\to W\to T$, with $V\to T$ proper by the assumed separatedness of $gf$, and $W\to T$ separated by base change and the representable compatibility in [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-cancellation] to obtain proper $V\to W$. The original $T\to D$ gives a section $s:T\to W$. Associativity of the 2-fibre product identifies $\mathcal A\times_D T$ with $V\times_W T$: its objects are precisely the objects of $\mathcal A$ together with their compatible identification with the given object of $D(T)$. Hence $\mathcal A\times_D T\to T$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. These are all scheme tests of $\Delta_f$, which is representable by [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry]. Thus $f$ is separated. Notice that the last pullback along $s$ is essential; $V\to W$ alone is not the test $\mathcal A\times_D T\to T$.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), proof of (3), with the cartesian square of Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map).

proof.text: Next suppose only that $p:I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is separated. By [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry], $I_{\mathcal B}$ is algebraic, $p$ is representable, and its identity section $e:\mathcal B\to I_{\mathcal B}$ is the second diagonal of $\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The representable compatibility in [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence] says that $\Delta_p:I_{\mathcal B}\to I_{\mathcal B}\times_{\mathcal B}I_{\mathcal B}$ is a closed immersion. The section $e$ is its base change along $(\mathrm{id},ep):I_{\mathcal B}\to I_{\mathcal B}\times_{\mathcal B}I_{\mathcal B}$: on any fibre, equality of an automorphism with the identity specifies exactly the neutral section. More explicitly the pullback object consists of $z,z'$ and isomorphisms $z'\simeq z$, $z'\simeq e(pz)$ compatible over $\mathcal B$; composition gives $z\simeq e(pz)$, and the inverse construction uses $z'=z$. Thus [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus] makes $e$ a closed immersion. Every scheme pullback of $e$ is therefore a closed immersion and is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. Under the second-diagonal identification this proves that $\Delta_{\mathcal B/k}$ is separated, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), implication (1)(a) to (1)(b); the section/diagonal pullback expands the forward implication of spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 06P6.

proof.text: If $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is finite, every scheme pullback is a finite scheme morphism and hence proper by [lem-sfb-affine-proper-finite]. It is in particular separated by the definition of scheme properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By the representable compatibility of [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence], $p$ is separated. Step 3 gives separated $\Delta_{\mathcal B/k}$. Apply steps 1--2 to $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $g:\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The composite is the separated structure map of $\mathcal A$, exactly the given hypothesis; consequently $\Delta_f$ is proper. No properness of $f$, representability of $f$, or separatedness of $\mathcal B$ was assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DUE (lemma-etale-local-finite-inertia), final separatedness argument; finite implies proper is morphisms.tex Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper).

lean.statement: theorem stack_separated_source_finite_inertia_target (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (B : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hA : IsAlgebraicModuliStack A) (hB : IsAlgebraicModuliStack B) (f : BasedFunctor A B) (hAsep : (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct (moduliBaseStructure A) (moduliBaseStructure A))), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange (moduliRelativeDiagonal (moduliBaseStructure A)) T t Z p ∧ MapIsProper (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨p⟩ : Z ⟶ schemeSpace T))) (hI : IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap (moduliInertiaProjection B)) : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct f f)), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange (moduliRelativeDiagonal f) T t Z p ∧ MapIsProper (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨p⟩ : Z ⟶ schemeSpace T)
lean.note: All three clauses are stated for general algebraic stacks, without a Deligne–Mumford or scheme-representability hypothesis. Separatedness is rendered by algebraic-space properness of every scheme base change of the canonical relative diagonal, using HasSpaceBaseChange and the existing AlgebraicSpace.MapIsProper. Finite inertia uses the existing IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap. No new notion is defined.
